rics.description: Core PCE price index- Actual, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Core PCE price index, month-over-month change — the Fed's PREFERRED inflation gauge against which the 2% target is officially measured. Released with BEA Personal Income & Outlays, ~2 weeks after CPI.
rics.how_to_use: Annualize the 6-month rate when reading FOMC commentary. ~0.17%/mo (~2% annualized) is target-consistent; sustained 0.3%+ prints are hawkish. Differs from core CPI in basket (less shelter weight, more healthcare) and chain-weighting.

rics.description: CPI, All items less food and energy
rics.meaning: Core CPI level — All items excluding food and energy. Strips out the two most volatile components, giving the cleanest read on underlying inflation pressure.
rics.how_to_use: Watch the YoY (aUSCPFYAR) for trend. Within core: shelter is ~40% of the index and the stickiest component; if shelter inflation slows, core decelerates with a lag. Used by analysts to call the Fed reaction function alongside core PCE.

rics.description: CPI, All items less food and energy
rics.meaning: Level of the Core CPI (consumer prices excluding food and energy) — the BLS measure of underlying inflation, stripped of the two most volatile components.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner inflation signal than headline CPI (strips out volatile food + energy). When core stays sticky while headline falls, inflation is broadening into services/shelter — harder to dislodge. The Fed monitors core CPI but officially targets core PCE; gaps between the two reflect basket weights (shelter is heavier in CPI).

rics.meaning: Month-over-month change in Core CPI — short-term underlying-inflation pulse.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner inflation signal than headline CPI (strips out volatile food + energy). When core stays sticky while headline falls, inflation is broadening into services/shelter — harder to dislodge. The Fed monitors core CPI but officially targets core PCE; gaps between the two reflect basket weights (shelter is heavier in CPI).

rics.meaning: Year-over-year change in Core CPI. Most-watched non-Fed-target inflation gauge: market reads first, Fed officials cross-reference with core PCE.
rics.how_to_use: Compare against Fed's 2% PCE target (CPI typically runs 30-50bp above PCE). >3% YoY is hot; <2.5% suggests Fed can ease. Decompose by shelter vs core services ex-shelter ('supercore') vs core goods to read the next move.

rics.description: PPI ex Food/Energy/Tr YY, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Year-over-year change in PPI — early signal of pipeline inflation pressures.
rics.how_to_use: Leads CPI for goods inflation. Watch core PPI (ex food/energy/trade) for the cleanest underlying signal. Final-demand services PPI is the input to core PCE.

rics.description: PPI ex Food/Energy/Trade MM, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Month-over-month change in PPI.
rics.how_to_use: Leads CPI for goods inflation. Watch core PPI (ex food/energy/trade) for the cleanest underlying signal. Final-demand services PPI is the input to core PCE.

rics.description: Producer Prices, Final demand less foods and energy, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Month-over-month change in PPI Final Demand — short-term producer-price pulse.
rics.how_to_use: Leads CPI by 1-3 months for goods inflation. Final-demand services PPI feeds directly into core PCE via the BEA's mapping. PPI spikes without CPI follow-through implies margin compression on producers.

rics.description: Producer Prices, Final demand less foods and energy, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Core PPI YoY — Producer Prices Final Demand less foods and energy. The producer-side equivalent of core CPI.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner pipeline-inflation signal than headline PPI. Tracks Core PCE goods inflation closely. Watch alongside USD trade-weighted: stronger USD lowers imported intermediate input costs.
